channel.title: IndieHOT — Indie Game Hot Topics
channel.description: IndieHOT collects indie game news from a set of public sources every day and scores it by rules: engines & tools, publishing & marketing, devlogs, industry & funding, events, reviews & postmortems. Only titles, one-line self-written summaries and outbound links are shown — no full text is republished.

item.title: Meta Quest Store Submission Guide for Developers
item.description: A practical guide for VR developers on getting through the Meta Horizon Store review, covering the performance, pause behaviour and data-declaration checks behind most rejections.

item.title: A walker, a horse, a car and a flying ray: movement in a WebGL2 engine where everything is code
item.description: Wallhammer Web, a browser 3D engine written entirely in code on plain WebGL2, gained a full movement system in 0.8.0/0.8.2; the author explains each piece, from walking to riding, driving, and flying.

item.title: Simple Python Overdrive Audio FX: Apply Overdrive to WAVs
item.description: A small Python script that adds guitar-pedal-style overdrive to WAV files, with drive and gain controls for giving game audio extra grit.

item.title: How to Host a Tombala Night at Home: An Organizer's Guide
item.description: A practical guide to hosting a Tombala game night at home, covering how this Turkish bingo-style game is played and run.

item.title: Beautiful Shimmering Veil In Blender Inspired By Foundation Title Sequence
item.description: Follow Marinko Tambur's tutorial to recreate the shimmering veil effect from the Foundation title sequence in Blender.

item.title: Excalibur 1.0: pause the game, keep the interface running
item.description: A walkthrough of Excalibur 1.0's pause system and migration tools, covering how to keep menus responsive while the game is paused and how to upgrade an existing TypeScript project.

item.title: Game Audio Format & Magic-Byte Compatibility Matrix (2026): FSB5, WEM, BNK, BFSTM, HCA & XWB
item.description: A 2026 reference table for identifying game audio containers from FMOD, Wwise, Nintendo and CRIWARE by their magic bytes, so you can pick the right decoder before trial and error.

item.title: Why our pool balls sped up mid-roll (and 3 other bugs from a browser pool game)
item.description: A postmortem of four unrelated bugs behind 'the physics feels wrong' in a hand-rolled three.js browser pool game: frame-rate-stepped physics, balls slipping through pocket mouths, AI freezing the game and shaders compiling mid-shot.

item.title: Game Audio Format & Magic-Byte Compatibility Matrix (2026): FSB5, WEM, BNK, BFSTM, HCA & XWB
item.description: A 2026 compatibility matrix of game audio formats and their magic bytes — FSB5, WEM, BNK, BFSTM, HCA, XWB — with an open-source CLI that works fully offline.

item.title: Grab the Best Black Friday Deals on 3D Tools, Assets & Courses
item.description: A roundup of Black Friday discounts on 3D tools, assets, and courses from Fab, the Unity Asset Store, Adobe, Reallusion, and more.

item.title: Curved ramps in a 2D physics engine, and the ball that looked like it was being hit 500 times a second
item.description: A devlog from the Rust physics engine Soliton on adding curved ramps properly — representing curves exactly so balls roll smoothly instead of bouncing hundreds of times a second.

item.title: I built a synthwave endless runner with Three.js
item.description: To learn 3D rendering, the author skipped the spinning-cube tutorial and built a neon-grid synthwave endless runner in the browser with Three.js — switch lanes, dodge obstacles, and it keeps speeding up.

item.title: Why AI Agents Silently Break Unreal Engine 5.9 Meshes: Projective-Radiometric Null-Space Drift (and How to Catch It Before Save)
item.description: AI agents can declare a mesh edit clean in the viewport and only reveal broken geometry, materials, or hair after saving — this piece breaks down why that silent damage happens and how to catch it before you hit save.

item.title: Generate a Maze With a Guaranteed Solution in Python (API Tutorial)
item.description: A maze generator written carelessly can easily produce an unsolvable level; this tutorial shows how to guarantee a valid path and expose the generator as an API for games.

item.title: Building a Dual-Engine Pixel & Smooth Vector Color-by-Number Studio in 83 KB (OKLab + Pure-JS PDF 1.4)
item.description: A fully browser-local color-by-number studio ships two rendering engines — pixel grid and smooth vector — in 83 KB, with photo conversion, vector PDF export and timelapse replay, and the post explains how the dual-engine split keeps it fast on mobile.

item.title: Can One Zero-DOM Skeleton Power Both a Tower Defense and a Mario-Style Action Platformer?
item.description: The author drives both a tower defense and a side-scrolling action platformer with a single TypeScript core fully decoupled from UI and rendering, testing how far a genre-agnostic gameplay skeleton can be reused.

item.title: You can't judge dialogue you never hear - run and debug it
item.description: Dialogue nobody has actually played through is untested; the author shows how to hear a whole conversation and step through it node by node inside the editor, no build required.

item.title: Until 20 Players Answer, Rarity Is Still a Guess: The Starter List in a Fan-Made Warm-Up
item.description: In a fan-made warm-up for a guess-the-rarest-answer game, rarity depends on answers players have already given, so the author explains how to set the starter list before enough players have answered.

item.title: I built a haunted map archive with Kiro
item.description: A browser game casts you as a haunted library's new Archivist, identifying fantasy worlds from maps with their names erased; the author recounts building it with Kiro.

item.title: Two snakes, one clock: the tick loop behind my real-time Snake Duel
item.description: Two snakes share a 24×18 grid and move on every tick, so the author breaks down the tick loop, the collision-check order, and the small decisions that keep the real-time duel fair.
